metadata.course: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: The AP Chemistry course framework: atomic structure and properties, compound structure and properties, properties of substances and mixtures, chemical reactions, kinetics, thermodynamics, equilibrium, acids and bases, and applications of thermodynamics.

id_namespace.reason: Concept ids are global; the prefix keeps this course disjoint from the shipped courses that share concept titles.

concepts.title: Acid-base definitions
concepts.summary: Brønsted-Lowry acids donate protons and bases accept them, and Lewis definitions generalise to electron pairs.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Acid-base reactions
concepts.summary: Proton transfer reactions neutralise acids and bases and can be followed by titration.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Acid-base titration curves
concepts.summary: A titration curve's shape and equivalence pH depend on the strength of the acid and base.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Bond enthalpies
concepts.summary: Breaking bonds costs energy and forming bonds releases it, which gives an estimate of reaction enthalpy.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Buffer capacity and selection
concepts.summary: A buffer works best near its pKa and within a limited capacity.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Buffers
concepts.summary: A weak acid and its conjugate base resist pH change by neutralising added acid or base.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Calculating equilibrium concentrations
concepts.summary: ICE tables track initial, change and equilibrium amounts to solve for concentrations.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Catalysis
concepts.summary: A catalyst provides a lower-energy path without being consumed, so it raises rate not yield.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Cell potential and standard reduction potentials
concepts.summary: Standard reduction potentials give the cell potential as cathode minus anode.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Colligative properties
concepts.summary: Vapour pressure, boiling point, freezing point and osmosis depend on particle count, not identity.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Collision theory and activation energy
concepts.summary: Molecules must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Concentration and molarity
concepts.summary: Molarity expresses moles of solute per litre of solution.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Coulomb's law and atomic structure
concepts.summary: The attraction between nucleus and electrons depends on charge and distance, which explains periodic trends.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Covalent bonding and Lewis structures
concepts.summary: Lewis structures show shared and lone pairs and predict bond order and geometry.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Determining rate laws from data
concepts.summary: Initial-rate and graphical methods extract orders and the rate constant.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Deviations from ideal behaviour
concepts.summary: Real gases deviate at high pressure and low temperature, where volume and attraction matter.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Dynamic equilibrium
concepts.summary: Forward and reverse rates become equal, so concentrations stop changing while reactions continue.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Electrolytic cells
concepts.summary: A non-spontaneous reaction can be driven by an external voltage.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Electron configuration
concepts.summary: Electrons fill orbitals in order of energy, following the aufbau principle and Hund's rule.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Endothermic and exothermic processes
concepts.summary: Energy is absorbed or released, and the sign of enthalpy change reports which.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Enthalpy of reaction and Hess's law
concepts.summary: Enthalpy is a state function, so reactions can be added to find an unknown enthalpy.

concepts.title: Entropy
concepts.summary: Entropy measures dispersal of energy and matter, and it tends to increase.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Faraday's laws and quantitative electrolysis
concepts.summary: Charge passed relates to moles of electrons and so to mass deposited.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Free energy and cell potential
concepts.summary: Cell potential is proportional to the free-energy change of the reaction.

concepts.title: Free energy and equilibrium
concepts.summary: The standard free-energy change is related to K, which links thermodynamics and equilibrium.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Galvanic cells
concepts.summary: A spontaneous redox reaction separated into half-cells produces a voltage.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Gibbs free energy
concepts.summary: Free energy combines enthalpy and entropy to decide thermodynamic favorability.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Heat capacity and calorimetry
concepts.summary: Calorimetry measures heat exchanged using mass, specific heat and temperature change.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Hybridisation and bonding models
concepts.summary: Mixing atomic orbitals explains observed geometries and bond angles.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Integrated rate laws and half-life
concepts.summary: Integrating the rate law gives concentration against time and the half-life for each order.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Intermolecular forces
concepts.summary: London dispersion, dipole-dipole and hydrogen bonding set boiling point and solubility.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Ionic bonding and lattice energy
concepts.summary: Lattice energy grows with charge and shrinks with ion size, which controls melting point and solubility.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Isotopes and average atomic mass
concepts.summary: An element's atomic mass is the abundance-weighted average of its isotopes.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Ka, Kb and conjugate pairs
concepts.summary: Ka and Kb of a conjugate pair multiply to the ion product of water.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Kinetic molecular theory
concepts.summary: Gas pressure and temperature follow from particle collisions and average kinetic energy.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.summary: A system at equilibrium shifts to partially oppose a change in concentration, pressure or temperature.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Mass spectrometry
concepts.summary: A mass spectrum measures isotope masses and abundances, which gives atomic mass and can identify a molecule.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Molecular structure and acid strength
concepts.summary: Bond polarity and stability of the conjugate base explain why some acids are stronger.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Moles and molar mass
concepts.summary: A mole is Avogadro's number of particles, which converts between mass and number of particles.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Net ionic equations
concepts.summary: Spectator ions are removed to show the species that actually change.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Oxidation-reduction reactions
concepts.summary: Electron transfer changes oxidation states, and half-reactions separate the two processes.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Percent yield
concepts.summary: Comparing actual with theoretical yield measures how complete and selective a reaction is.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Periodic trends
concepts.summary: Atomic radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity and electronegativity follow from nuclear charge and shielding.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: pH and pOH
concepts.summary: pH is the negative logarithm of hydrogen-ion concentration, and pH plus pOH is fourteen at 25 degrees.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Phase changes and phase diagrams
concepts.summary: Heating and pressure change the balance of phases, which a phase diagram maps.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Photoelectron spectroscopy
concepts.summary: A photoelectron spectrum reports the binding energy of each electron shell and subshell.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Polarity and dipole moments
concepts.summary: Polar bonds plus an asymmetric shape produce a net dipole, which controls intermolecular forces.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Rate laws and reaction order
concepts.summary: The rate law is determined by experiment, and its orders need not match the stoichiometric coefficients.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Reaction mechanisms
concepts.summary: A mechanism is a sequence of elementary steps whose slowest step sets the overall rate.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Reaction rate
concepts.summary: Rate is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Resonance and formal charge
concepts.summary: Resonance spreads electrons over several positions, and formal charge selects the best structure.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Separating mixtures
concepts.summary: Distillation, filtration and chromatography separate by differing physical properties.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Solids, liquids and gases
concepts.summary: The kinetic energy of particles relative to intermolecular forces decides the state.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Solubility equilibria and Ksp
concepts.summary: A solubility product describes the equilibrium between a solid and its ions.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Solutions and solubility
concepts.summary: Like dissolves like, and solubility depends on temperature and pressure.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.summary: Absorbance is proportional to concentration and path length, which allows concentration to be measured.

concepts.summary: Mole ratios from the balanced equation give theoretical yield, and the limiting reactant caps it.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: Strong acids and bases
concepts.summary: Strong acids and bases ionise completely, so concentration directly gives the ion concentration.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: The Arrhenius equation
concepts.summary: Rate constants rise with temperature in a way that reveals activation energy.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: The equilibrium constant K
concepts.summary: K expresses the ratio of products to reactants at equilibrium and its size reports the extent of reaction.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation
concepts.summary: pH depends on pKa and the ratio of conjugate base to acid, which is the buffer calculation.

concepts.title: The ideal gas law
concepts.summary: Pressure, volume, temperature and moles are linked by PV equals nRT.

provenance.source: AP Chemistry - Structure, Reactions and Thermodynamics

concepts.title: The mole and empirical formulae
concepts.summary: Percentage composition converts to a mole ratio, which gives the empirical formula.

concepts.summary: Non-standard concentrations change cell potential in a way the Nernst equation predicts.

concepts.title: Weak acid and base equilibria

concepts.summary: Atoms are conserved, so coefficients must balance every element.
